title: Chemistry Grade 11 Practice Questions 2018 (12 chapters combined)
description: Combined 12 chapter files (C2018_G11U1_R1.json, C2018_G11U1_R2.json, C2018_G11U2_R1.json, C2018_G11U2_R2.json, C2018_G11U3_R1.json, C2018_G11U3_R2.json, C2018_G11U4_R1.json, C2018_G11U4_R2.json, C2018_G11U5_R1.json, C2018_G11U5_R2.json, C2018_G11U6_R1.json, C2018_G11U6_R2.json) into one exam. 58 total questions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following laws states that every chemical compound contains constant mass ratio of its composing elements?
questions.explanation: The Law of Definite Proportion states that a compound always contains its elements in a fixed mass ratio.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is CORRECT about atoms based on modern atomic theory?
options: Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass number.
Atoms of the same element are the same in all their properties.
Atoms can be created during ordinary chemical reaction.
Atoms of different elements can be the same atoms.
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, so they have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.

questions.questionText: The electronic configuration of an atom is, 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p¹. Which type of electronic rearrangement should the atom undergo to form a stable chemical bond?
options: The atom has to lose three electrons from its 3s and 3p orbital.
The atom has to gain five electrons on its 3p orbital.
The atom has to gain one electron on its 3p orbital.
The atom has to lose one electron from its 3p orbital.
questions.explanation: The atom has 3 valence electrons, so it loses 3 electrons to achieve a stable noble-gas configuration.

questions.questionText: Which of the following terms represent particles of light?
questions.explanation: Photons are the particles (quanta) of light.

questions.questionText: Which type of radioactive emission is deflected by a negatively charged plate?
questions.explanation: Alpha particles are positively charged, so they are attracted to and deflected by a negative plate.

questions.questionText: What is the energy of hydrogen electron when n = 2? (R_H = 2.18 x 10⁻¹⁸ J)
Which of the following is the CORRECT description of Aufbau's principle?
options: Degenerate orbitals are occupied by single electrons before pairing with electrons of opposite spin.
Electrons occupy the lowest energy orbital available before entering the higher energy orbital.
Electronic transition from higher energy to lower energy orbitals results in the release of energy.
The four quantum numbers cannot be identical for any two electrons in a given atom.
questions.explanation: Aufbau's principle states that electrons fill lower-energy orbitals before higher-energy orbitals.

questions.questionText: In a reaction, 130 g of zinc reacts with 64 g of sulfur and produces 194 g of a white powder of zinc sulfide. Which of the following is illustrated by this reaction?
options: The law of conservation of mass
questions.explanation: Mass of reactants = 130 + 64 = 194 g, equal to the product mass. This demonstrates conservation of mass.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the electron configuration of Gallium (Z=31)?
questions.explanation: Gallium has 31 electrons. Filling orbitals gives [Ar] 3d¹⁰4s²4p¹, matching option D.

questions.questionText: A student added 31 g Na₂CO₃ to CH₃COOH weighing 39.4 g. The two substances reacted and released 13 g of CO₂ to the atmosphere and the contents of the reaction vessel weighed 57.4 g. What fundamental law does this experiment demonstrate?
options: The law of conservation of mass
questions.explanation: Reactants = 31 + 39.4 = 70.4 g. Products = 57.4 + 13 = 70.4 g. Equal masses demonstrate conservation of mass.

questions.questionText: Which of the following emitted particles that could NOT be deflected by electric field were produced when a thin foil of beryllium was bombarded with α-particles?
questions.explanation: Neutrons have no electric charge, so an electric field cannot deflect them.

questions.questionText: Which atomic model uses s, p, d and f sublevels for each allowed main energy levels?
questions.explanation: The quantum mechanical model divides principal energy levels into s, p, d and f sublevels and orbitals.

questions.questionText: What is the CORRECT explanation for the fact that CCl₄ is a non-polar molecule, while CHCl₃ is a polar molecule?
options: The polarity of C-H bond is greater than the polarity of C-Cl bond.
CCl₄ has no polar bonds while CHCl₃ has one polar bond.
The bond polarities in C-Cl bonds of CCl₄ have cancelled each other but not in the case of CHCl₃.
The bond polarities in C-Cl bonds of CHCl₃ have cancelled each other but not in the case of CCl₄.
questions.explanation:
CCl₄ is symmetrical, so its bond dipoles cancel. 

CHCl₃ is not symmetrical, so the dipoles do not completely cancel.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the favorable condition for the formation of an ionic bond?
options: metal with low ionization energy and a non-metal with low electron affinity.
metal with high ionization energy and a non-metal with high electron affinity.
metal with high ionization energy and a non-metal with low electron affinity.
metal with low ionization energy and non-metal with high electron affinity.
questions.explanation: A metal should easily lose electrons (low ionization energy), while a non-metal should readily gain electrons (high electron affinity).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is CORRECT about the general properties of ionic compounds?
options: They have high melting and low boiling point
They are insoluble in polar solvents
questions.explanation: Strong electrostatic forces hold ions in a rigid lattice, making ionic compounds hard but brittle.

questions.questionText: Which of the following represents the group and period, of an element based on the electronic configuration of 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p³ respectively?
questions.explanation:
The highest shell is n = 3 → Period 3.

 There are 5 valence electrons → Group VA (15).

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements CORRECTLY defines chemical bonding?
options: It is a force that holds atoms together in a compound.
It is the repulsive force between similar charges.
It is the process taking place during the evaporation of a compound.
It is a kind of chemical reaction taking place in matter.
questions.explanation: Chemical bonding is the attractive force that holds atoms or ions together in a compound.

questions.questionText: What is the bond order of He₂ molecule?
questions.explanation:
Bond order = ½(N_b − N_a) =
 ½(2 − 2) = 0.
 Therefore, He₂ has no stable bond.

questions.questionText: The electronic configuration of an atom is, 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p¹. Which type of electronic rearrangement should the atom undergo to form a stable chemical bond?
options: The atom has to lose three electrons from its 3s and 3p orbital.
The atom has to gain five electrons on its 3p orbital.
The atom has to gain one electron on its 3p orbital.
The atom has to lose one electron from its 3p orbital.
questions.explanation: The atom has 3 valence electrons, so it loses 3 electrons to achieve a stable noble-gas configuration.

questions.questionText:
Consider an incomplete molecular orbital energy level diagram for H₂ molecule:

Which of the following representations is CORRECT to complete the given diagram?
options: = σ₁ₛ, B = σ*₁ₛ, C = 1s, and D = 1s
= σ₁ₛ, B = σ₁ₛ, C = σ*₁ₛ, and D = σ*₁ₛ
= 1s, B = σ₁ₛ, C = σ₁ₛ, and D = 1s
= 1s, B = 1s, C = σ*₁ₛ, and D = σ₁ₛ
questions.explanation:
A and B are hydrogen 1s atomic orbitals. 

The higher MO is antibonding σ*₁ₛ (C), while the lower MO is bonding σ₁ₛ (D).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the CORRECT Lewis structure of the molecule of FCN?
questions.explanation:
FCN has 16 valence electrons.

 The structure F–C≡N gives all atoms complete octets with the most appropriate formal charges.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a three dimensional, well-defined and ordered structure of a solid material?
questions.explanation: A crystal has a regular, repeating three-dimensional arrangement of particles.

questions.questionText: Which of the following reaction schemes represents the formation of coordinate covalent bond?
questions.explanation: A coordinate covalent bond forms when one atom provides both electrons in the shared pair.

questions.questionText: Consider the following diagram of the molecule of PCl₅: From this diagram, what is the hybridization of the central atom, P?
questions.explanation:
PCl₅ has 5 bonding pairs and trigonal bipyramidal geometry.

 Therefore, its hybridization is sp³d.

questions.questionText:
Given the following data for the reaction of lithium metal with fluorine gas:

Li(s) + ½ F₂(g) → LiF(s), ΔH_LiF = -594.1 KJ

I. Li(s) → Li(g)                ΔH₁ = 155.7 KJ

II. F₂(g) → 2 F(g)           ΔH₂ = 150.6 KJ

III. Li(g) → Li⁺(g) + e⁻       ΔH₃ = 520 KJ

IV. F(g) + e⁻ → F⁻(g)          ΔH₄ = -328 KJ

What is the lattice energy of lithium fluoride, LiF crystal?
Which of the following obeys the octet rule for all of its constituent atoms?
questions.explanation: In CCl₄, carbon and all chlorine atoms have complete octets. The other species contain expanded octets.

questions.questionText: The octet rule is violated by some molecules. What is the reason for the violation of the octet rule?
options: Molecules with eight or eighteen electrons on the central atom
Molecules with less than or more than eight electrons on the central atom
Molecules with eighteen electrons on the central atom
Molecules with eight electrons on the central atom
questions.explanation: The octet rule is violated when the central atom has fewer than or more than 8 valence electrons, such as BF₃ or SF₆.

questions.questionText: Which of the following compounds contains a coordinate covalent bond? (Given Atomic Number: H = 1, C = 6, N = 7, O = 8, P = 15, S = 16, F = 9 and Cl = 17)
questions.explanation: NH₄⁺ forms when NH₃ donates its lone pair to H⁺, creating a coordinate covalent bond. Therefore, NH₄NO₃ contains such a bond.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following table of three molecules: Water, Methane and Ammonia 

Even though there are four electron pairs around the central atom of each molecule, there is a variation in bond angle and geometry.

 What is the cause of the variation observed?
options: The difference in repulsion forces between the electron pairs on the central atom
The difference in attraction forces between the electron pairs on the central atom
The electron affinity difference between the central atoms
The electronegativity difference between the central atoms
questions.explanation: VSEPR theory states that electron pairs repel each other. Lone pairs repel more strongly than bonding pairs, changing bond angles and shapes.

questions.questionText: The hybridization of the central atom in the molecular ion of tetrachloroiodate (ICl₄⁻) is sp³d². What is the geometrical shape of ICl₄⁻?
questions.explanation: ICl₄⁻ has 6 electron domains: 4 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs. The lone pairs occupy opposite positions, giving a square planar shape.

questions.questionText: The distance between the centers of atoms in covalent molecules is called bond length. Which one of the following is the CORRECT increasing order of carbon-oxygen bond length?
questions.explanation: Higher bond order means a shorter bond. Therefore: C≡O < C=O < C-O.

questions.questionText: Which type of intermolecular forces are the only forces that exist between noble gas atoms and non-polar molecules?
questions.explanation: Non-polar molecules and noble gases have no permanent dipoles, so their intermolecular attraction is due to London dispersion forces.

questions.questionText: What is the bond order of the peroxide ion, O₂²⁻?
questions.explanation: For O₂²⁻, bond order = (bonding electrons − antibonding electrons)/2 = (10 − 8)/2 = 1.

questions.questionText: Which type of bond is formed when one atom donates both electrons of the bond in a covalent bonding?
questions.explanation: A dative or coordinate covalent bond forms when one atom supplies both shared electrons.

questions.questionText: In which of the following molecules do dipole-dipole forces exist?
questions.explanation: HCl is a polar molecule, so permanent dipole-dipole attractions exist between its molecules.

questions.questionText: What kind of intermolecular forces are present when polar molecules come close to one another?
questions.explanation: Polar molecules have permanent dipoles that attract each other through dipole-dipole forces.

questions.questionText: Which of the following processes is the reverse of fusion during a phase change of a substance?
questions.explanation:
Fusion is solid → liquid.

 Its reverse is liquid → solid, called freezing or crystallization.

questions.questionText:
Consider the diagram below:

Which of the following statements is the CORRECT conclusion about the given reaction diagram?
options: Enthalpy of the reaction shows an energy release.
Enthalpy of the reaction (ΔH) has positive value.
Enthalpy of the reactant and the product are equal.
Enthalpy of the reaction (ΔH) has negative value.
questions.explanation:
Products have higher enthalpy than reactants, so ΔH = H_products − H_reactants > 0.

 The reaction is endothermic.

questions.questionText: If 2 L of Ne gas at 100 °C is cooled at constant pressure until the volume becomes 1.5 L, then what is the final temperature?
Why do gases easily flow and diffuse through one another? This is because of
options: gases move freely and randomly throughout a given space.
the particles of gases are rigidly held in position by strong forces.
the particles of gases are very close to each other.
high intermolecular forces exist between the particles of gases.
questions.explanation: Gas particles move freely and randomly with weak intermolecular attractions, allowing gases to flow and diffuse.

questions.questionText: A sample of gas at 27 °C and 1.0 atm has a volume of 5.0 L. What volume will the gas occupy if the temperature is doubled and the pressure is kept constant?
questions.explanation: Using the intended interpretation in the options, 27°C → 54°C: V₂ = 5.0 × 327.15/300.15 ≈ 5.45 L.

questions.questionText: A hypothetical gas that shows simple relationship between temperature, pressure, volume and amount of substance is called _____.
questions.explanation: An ideal gas follows PV = nRT and has a simple relationship among pressure, volume, temperature and amount.

questions.questionText: Under what conditions does the behavior of a real gas obey the ideal gas laws?
options: At low temperature and high pressure
At low temperature and low pressure
At high temperature and high pressure
At high temperature and low pressure
questions.explanation: High temperature reduces the effect of attractions, and low pressure makes molecular volume less significant. Thus, gases behave most ideally under these conditions.

questions.questionText:
Given the following heating curve:

In which region of the heating curve does heating of the liquid raises its temperature until the boiling point is reached?
questions.explanation: C to D represents heating the liquid, so its temperature rises until it reaches the boiling point.

questions.questionText: Which of the following terms is defined as 'how fast a solute goes into solution'?
questions.explanation: Rate of dissolution is the speed at which a solute dissolves in a solvent.

questions.questionText: What is a reaction rate? It is
options: the state in chemical system where concentration of products remains constant.
the reactant that is entirely consumed when a reaction goes to completion.
the increase in molar concentration of the product of a reaction per unit time.
the minimum energy of collision required for two molecules to react.
questions.explanation: Reaction rate is the change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time.

questions.questionText:
A student performed the following experiment during his laboratory session:
First: He added 25 mL of 2.0 M hydrochloric acid in each of two beakers
Second: He added 2.0 g of calcium to the first beaker
Third: He added 2.0 g of iron to the second beaker
Which of the following will be his observation?
options: It is not possible to observe any difference in reaction between the two beakers
The rates of chemical reaction in the first and second beakers are identical
fast chemical reaction is observed in the second beaker
fast chemical reaction is observed in the first beaker
questions.explanation: Calcium is much more reactive than iron, so it reacts faster and more vigorously with HCl.

questions.questionText: How does a catalyst speed up a chemical reaction without being consumed itself?
options: By providing a new pathway that increases temperature of reaction
By providing a new pathway that decreases temperature of reaction
By providing a new pathway that increases activation energy
By providing a new pathway that decreases activation energy
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy, increasing the reaction rate.

questions.questionText:
Given an equilibrium reaction:
H₂S (g) + I₂ (s) ⇌ 2HI (g) + S (s)
At equilibrium, the partial pressure of H₂S and HI are 1.6 atm, 2.0 x 10⁻² atm at 71 °C respectively. What is the value of the equilibrium constant, Kp of this reaction?
questions.explanation:
Solids are omitted: 
Kp = (P_HI)²/P_H₂S =
 (2.0×10⁻²)²/1.6 =
 2.5×10⁻⁴.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a factor that affects a reaction at chemical equilibrium?
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally, so it does not change the equilibrium position.

questions.questionText:
Given the equilibrium reaction:
2SO₃(g) ⇌ 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g)
At certain temperature, the equilibrium concentration of SO₃, SO₂ and O₂ are 0.4 M, 0.2 M and 0.1 M respectively. What is the value of the equilibrium constant for this reaction?
The synthesis of ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen is known to be an exothermic reaction. What steps will increase the yield of ammonia?
options: Decreasing the pressure while increasing the temperature of the system.
Increasing the pressure while decreasing the temperature of the system.
Decreasing the pressure and temperature of the system.
Increasing the pressure and temperature of the system.
questions.explanation:
N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ is exothermic and has fewer gas moles on the product side.

 Higher pressure and lower temperature favor NH₃ formation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following organic compounds is prepared by the elimination of water molecule from two alcohol molecules with a strong dehydrating agent such as concentrated sulfuric acid at a temperature of 140 °C?
questions.explanation:
Two alcohol molecules undergo intermolecular dehydration at 140 °C:
 2R–OH → R–O–R + H₂O.
 The product is an ether.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is CORRECT for the oxidation of aldehydes and ketones?
options: Ketones are readily oxidized to yield carboxylic acids.
Aldehydes are readily oxidized to yield carboxylic acids.
Ketones are readily oxidized to yield ester.
Aldehydes are generally inert towards oxidation.
questions.explanation: Aldehydes are easily oxidized to carboxylic acids, while ketones resist mild oxidation.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following structure of an organic compound:    
  CH₃
       |
CH₃CH—O—CH₂CH₃

    What is the CORRECT name of the given organic compound?
questions.explanation:
The parent chain is propane and the ethoxy group is attached to carbon 2. 

Therefore, the name is 2-ethoxypropane.

questions.questionText: Which of the following compounds is a triester of glycerol?
questions.explanation: Fats are triglycerides: triesters formed from glycerol and three fatty acids.

questions.questionText: What is the molecular formula of pentyl butyrate?
questions.explanation: Butyrate has 4 carbons and pentyl has 5 carbons: CH₃CH₂CH₂COOCH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃.

questions.questionText:
What is the IUPAC nomenclature for the following monohydric alcohol?
CH₃-CH(CH₃)-CH(OH)-CH₂-CH(CH₂-CH₃)-CH₃
questions.explanation: Choose the longest chain containing –OH: 7 carbons. Numbering from the nearest end gives OH at C3 and methyl groups at C2 and C5: 2,5-dimethyl-3-heptanol.
